documents.unit: Artificial Intelligence at PCC (college AI site)
documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at PCC
documents.summary: The college's AI landing page states a conditional welcome of AI, says PCC has no specific AI policy yet and relies on existing board policies for interim guidance, and leaves course expectations to instructors. It also offers faculty support.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule of its own: "Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class" and "PCC does not yet have any specific Artificial Intelligence policy", so the decision is handed to instructors.

units.why: The college states its general stance toward AI: it "embraces emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), to the extent that they advance this mission". This is an institution-level framework statement (P56), not a per-course rule, and it welcomes AI conditionally.
units.anchor: PCC embraces emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), to the extent that they advance

units.why: The sentence sets conditions on AI: it "must do so in ways that center students, uphold equity, and respect the professional judgment of faculty". It is a principle in the institutional framework (P56); equity (P51) is only one of three principles so P56 fits best.
units.anchor: center students, uphold equity, and respect the professional judgment of faculty
units.frag_start: AI may enhance teaching and learning

units.why: "Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class" hands the decision to the instructor, which is P04, addressed to all because it explains who decides.
units.anchor: determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class

units.why: Students are told to "Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor" to learn the rules, which directs students to ask the instructor rather than assume (P10).
units.anchor: Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor.

units.why: "PCC supports faculty in integrating AI into their teaching thoughtfully and on their own terms" and offers consultations; this is institutional support for faculty learning about AI (P63), and "on their own terms" also signals faculty autonomy.
units.anchor: PCC supports faculty in integrating AI into their teaching thoughtfully and on their own terms.

units.why: "PCC does not yet have any specific Artificial Intelligence policy" with "board-approved policies in place that are applicable" for "interim guidance": existing policies (academic integrity, conduct, IT use, privacy, proprietary content, accessibility) govern AI. P77 (comply with existing policy) fits best; the word "interim" also signals provisional status.
units.anchor: board-approved policies in place that are applicable and can offer immediate interim guidance
units.fit_note: Also says the college has no specific AI policy yet and the guidance is interim (P54); the type captures only the reliance on existing policies.

documents.unit: Artificial Intelligence at PCC (college AI site)
documents.title: Student learning and AI
documents.summary: Student-facing page that sends students to their instructor for course rules, states that uncited AI text violates the Student Code of Conduct, advises on data protection in PCC-provided tools, and lists support and appeal routes.
documents.stance_why: It repeats "Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor" and so delegates; the only rule it states itself is that uncited AI text is a conduct violation, which does not set a general stance.

units.why: "Expectations for AI use in a course are determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class" delegates the decision to each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class

units.why: Students are told to "Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor", so they should ask the instructor about the rule (P10).
units.anchor: Check your syllabus and talk to your instructor.

units.why: "Using AI-generated text without citation is a violation under Article IV of the Student Code of Conduct" classifies uncited AI text as misconduct (P36). P24 (disclose) also applies, but the statement frames the consequence as a conduct violation, so P36 fits best.
units.anchor: Using AI-generated text without citation is a violation under Article IV
units.fit_note: Also implies AI-generated text must be cited (P24), and the rule is stated for text only, not code.

units.why: The page lists "AI literacy: Understanding what AI is, how it works, and its limitations" as a resource offered to students, which is an AI-literacy offering (P70).
units.anchor: Understanding what AI is, how it works, and its limitations.

units.why: "Always consider how to protect your data when using AI applications" tells students to guard their data (P50).
units.anchor: Always consider how to protect your data when using AI applications.

units.why: "PCC-provided tools have been vetted by the PCC Information Security team" and "your content is not used to train any models": this describes vetted tools and data protection (P50).
units.anchor: PCC-provided tools have been vetted by the PCC Information Security team.

units.why: "you retain ownership of your materials" in PCC-provided tools states who owns inputs, which is ownership of AI inputs (P52).
units.anchor: you retain ownership of your materials

units.why: The page names "Google Gemini" and "Gemini Notebook" as the PCC-provided AI tools, a sanctioned college tool (P17); it does not say they are the only tools allowed.
units.fit_note: The page only names the tools; it does not state conditions or exclusivity.

units.why: Students with questions on responsible use, citing AI or fit to an assignment are told to "Contact a faculty librarian"; this points to human help (P72).
units.anchor: Contact a faculty librarian in person at the library

units.why: For help with how a specific tool works students are sent to the "Student Help Desk", which is human support for tools (P72).
units.frag_start: Can I get help with how

units.why: "What if my use of AI impacted my grade? Speak with your instructor or use the grade appeal process" gives students a route to contest a grade; closest is P64 (right to respond), though it concerns grades generally.
units.anchor: Speak with your instructor or use the grade appeal process
units.frag_start: What if my use of AI
units.fit_note: Concerns a grade affected by AI use, not strictly an AI-misuse allegation.

units.why: "What if I have been unfairly accused or treated regarding my use of AI? ... use the formal complaint process" gives students recourse against unfair AI accusations (P64).
units.anchor: unfairly accused or treated regarding my use of AI

notes: Course layer deferred in the collect file; no school or computing document found. Both documents delegate to instructors. One sentence about PCC-provided tools is split into separate units on distinct claims (vetting vs ownership).
